blocks.text: Which capital structure should {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} take to lenders?

Since the engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}, we have reconciled the model to the monthly accounts and drafted the financing memorandum as far as the business description. The memorandum cannot be finished, and no financing source can be approached, until the shareholders choose the structure we will market, because the list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}} we have prepared divides between banks and other senior lenders on one side and funds providing junior capital on the other. A decision this month keeps outreach on the timetable in our engagement letter.
Our answer: market a senior facility and a junior tranche together

items: Precedent. In the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.comparators}} we reviewed for industrial and business-services companies of similar size, senior lenders seldom went as far as the total the shareholders have in mind, and junior capital usually covered the difference.
Cash flow. The model shows cash generation weighted to the second half of the year, and the amortization a senior-only facility would require falls hardest in the months when cash is thinnest.
Cost and control. Junior capital costs more than bank debt, but it asks for little or no amortization, and on the terms we expect it can be arranged without warrants or a board seat.
The existing bank. A senior facility of conventional size leaves the existing bank room to bid, and its knowledge of the company is worth keeping in the process.
One round. Marketing both pieces at once lets each lender price against the whole structure, so the shareholders see the real trade-off between cost and covenants before they commit.

blocks.text: What we need from the shareholders to proceed

The draft memorandum and the proposed source list went to Robert Grimes with this deck, and both are written on the assumption that the recommendation is accepted. Before our working session later this month we ask the shareholders for a decision on the structure, their comments on the draft memorandum, and approval of the source list, with any additions or exclusions marked on it. Heather Delacruz will take the shareholders through the recommendation in person if that would help, Sarah Fletcher will begin first calls only once the list is approved, and questions on the model should come to Robert Turner.
